doc.title: Houston Person Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 2, 1998 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Music in schools and his children
summary: Asked about Lincoln Center, Person says nothing is bad but wants more music in schools, and briefly mentions his stepson and a daughter who wants to be a promoter.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: Do you think institutions like Lincoln Center Jazz are good or bad for music overall?

Well nothing is bad. I mean nothing is bad. Even if you’re creating music for 20 or 30 people or for a private soiree, nothing’s bad. I’d just like to see more music in the schools. That’s where it all starts. Like we used to have the music appreciation courses and you know, where you just got a little whiff of music, you didn’t have to be a virtuoso, just know the alternatives. And that’s what we had, we had music appreciation classes in early school. And then if you wanted to be in the band they had an instrument for you, no matter how broken it was, they had one for you. And there are a lot of schools that do that but there’s just not enough. It doesn’t reach — especially in the inner cities. Now they’re even trying to cut out athletic programs. So you really stymie childrens’ creative ability when they don’t have any artistic things. But still I don’t know how the parents let the administrations get away with it, when they pay taxes.
I know education is a big issue for you, central to your philosophy. Do you get involved with — your son is at college now is that right?
And does he seem to be finding his way in his college life? Are you happy with what he’s doing?
Yeah. But he’s not — he likes music, I think eventually he will wind up with some of that. And I have a daughter who wants to be a promoter.
She can start with you, right? © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-
